⛔ SNG-491. THE DEATH TRADITION — DOMAIN BEFORE SKILLS. Erik: 'it's the death tradition (now with emotion), but it also is very much a user of SPIRIT/SOUL MANIPULATION. NECROMANCY has a home here — it needs to be a school at least. I want to get the whole DOMAIN AND TRADITION correct before we evaluate the skills PROPERLY.'
⚠️ HE IS RIGHT AND I WAS AUDITING BEFORE KNOWING WHAT THE TRADITION IS — the same error as judging a project skill on scene frequency. §37 now says measure first; it should also say UNDERSTAND FIRST.

theThesis._statement:
⛔ DEATH IS THE TRADITION OF WHAT PERSISTS AFTER AN ENDING. That is the one idea under all three of its schools, and it is what makes ashwarden and threnodist one people rather than two filed together.
   THE BODY ends — and something remains that can be set to work, questioned, or walked back for.
   THE PERSON ends — and something remains that has an address, can be named, and can be reached.
   THE GRIEF does not end — and it is the most durable thing any of them handle.
⚠️ THE ASHWARDEN ETHIC IS 'TENDING THE END'. THE THRENODIST ETHIC IS 'REFUSING TO LET GO BE THE SAME AS FORGET'. ⛔ THOSE ARE TWO ANSWERS TO ONE QUESTION: WHAT DO WE OWE WHAT HAS ENDED?
theThesis._whyEmotionBelongs: ⚠️ Grief looked like a separate tradition bolted on. It is not. ⛔ CARRIED NAME AND NAMES OF THE LOST ARE SOUL-WORK PERFORMED THROUGH FEELING — holding the dead present, correctly, against the softening. A Threnodist singing the names and an Ashwarden asking the dead a question are reaching for the same thing by different means.
theThesis._whyNecromancyBelongs: ⛔ IT IS NOT A DARK CORNER OF THE TRADITION — IT IS THE TRADITION'S CENTRAL CLAIM MADE PHYSICAL. If something persists after an ending, it can be addressed. Set Hand addresses a body, Ask the Dead addresses a person, Calling Back walks the road both ways. ⚠️ THE PALELANDS 'HAVE NEVER PRETENDED OTHERWISE' — that line is already in Set Hand and it is the tradition being honest.

Palework._what: ⛔ ENDING THINGS, AND TENDING THE END. The craft the tradition is named for: bring a failing thing to its end sooner, hold one exactly where it is, ward an ending that should not happen, or read what is failing and how long it has.
Palework._note: ⚠️ Nine, all ashwarden. Holds both the tradition's gentlest craft (Kept Vigil) and its worst (The Cut Thread).

Necromancy._what: ⛔ WHAT REMAINS OF A PERSON, ADDRESSED. Question the recently dead, set a finished body to work, draw vitality out of the living, walk where death has been, and — rarely — reach into the dark and bring someone back.
Necromancy._note: ⛔ ERIK'S RULING: 'NECROMANCY HAS A HOME HERE — IT NEEDS TO BE A SCHOOL AT LEAST.' ⚠️ Seven crafts, all ashwarden, and it is where SOUL STARE belongs — 'everything has an essence (address)' is the necromantic thesis stated as a mechanic.

Threnody._what: ⛔ WHAT THE LIVING CARRY, AND WHAT IS OWED TO IT. Take grief off someone, spread it across many, hold the dead present by name, strike with a feeling that cannot be closed off, or give a feeling a form that outlasts the singer.
Threnody._note: ⚠️ Twelve, all threnodist. The largest school and the one most in need of merging.
